newsitem.title: CHINA: SHENZHEN B INDEX CLOSES UP 3.15 PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: SHENZHEN B INDEX CLOSES UP 3.15 PERCENT.

text.p: Shenzhen's B index closed substantially higher on Wednesday, boosted by strong buying in Shenzhen Petrochemical (Holdings) Co Ltd and other stocks expected to post good interim results, analysts said.
The hard currency index surged 4.20 points or 3.15 percent to 137.44, while turnover ballooned to HK$103 million from Tuesday's HK$59 million.
The yuan-denominated A share index fell 9.55 points or 2.51 percent to 370.86 on light turnover of 3.2 billion yuan against Tuesday's 4.2 billion.
"Shenzhen Petrochemical and other stocks with good first half expectations grabbed the market focus today," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
The issue closed at its 10 percent limit-up level of HK$2.53 as 130,288 shares changed hands.
Shenzhen-listed companies must release their 1997 interim reports by the end of this month, but only eight out of the 49 B share companies have so far made public their results.
Market giant Bengang Steel Plates, the most actively traded stock, extended recent gains and helped to lift the index, analysts said.
Bengang closed up HK$0.13 at HK$2.35, still short of its issue price of HK$2.38. Volume reached 6.9 million shares.
Analysts said they expected further gains as the index makes up losses resulting from measures by the government to cool speculation in May.
"There is...very little room for the B index to fall," an analyst at J&A Securities said.

In the past three months, B share prices have lost nearly 30 percent on both the Shenzhen and Shanghai stock exchanges after hitting year highs in mid-May when Beijing began to crack down on what it saw as overheated markets.
The A share market continued to tumble, plagued by worse-than-expected interim reports, analysts said.
Market leader Shenzhen Development Bank recently said its 1997 earnings growth had slowed. Analysts said they were gloomy about its first half results.
The stock fell 0.80 yuan to 30.71 yuan on volume of 7.0 million shares.
